source.version: Published proceedings version, Proceedings of the Design Society, Volume 5: ICED25, pp. 479–488; complete local PDF and markdown conversion.
source.title_on_document: AI-powered inventive design: idea funnelling, concept creation, and hybrid problem-solving teams

paper_design_summary: The authors operated ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-o1, and Gemini Advanced on mechanical engineering design problems, including a twist-off screw cap, in a unified series of workflow comparisons. Five concept-creation approaches were applied sequentially to the AI-agents; no allocation of people to assistance conditions is described (PDF pp. 3–4, printed pp. 481–482, section 3 and Table 1). AI-generated concepts received self-evaluations and cross-evaluations for usefulness, feasibility, complexity, and novelty, combined into a weighted Total Value, and the agents selected the strongest concepts (PDF pp. 7–9, printed pp. 485–487, Table 6, equation (1), and section 5).

studies.label: AI idea-funnelling workflows across engineering design cases

assignment.what_was_assigned: No assignment of people to generative-AI assistance conditions is reported. The AI-agents underwent five concept-creation approaches sequentially; the within structure describes repeated AI workflows, not repeated human participant conditions.
assignment.quote: Five distinct concept creation approaches were employed sequentially (as detailed in Table 1), each demanding the AI-agent produce and evaluate five new solution concepts.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 482), section 3, Phase 4 and Table 1; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 481), section 3, identifies the authors as the human operators.

arms.name: Approach 1
arms.description: AI-agent merges different complementary ideas to address the problem. Workflow condition, not a group of people (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

arms.name: Approach 2
arms.description: AI-agent creates concepts using core solution ideas selected by the AI-agent. Workflow condition, not a group of people (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

arms.name: Approach 3
arms.description: AI-agent creates concepts using core solution ideas selected by the human operator. Workflow condition, not a group of people (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

arms.name: Approach 4
arms.description: AI-agent enhances human-selected core ideas with complementary ideas selected by the AI-agent. Workflow condition, not a group of people (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

arms.name: Approach 5
arms.description: AI-agent creates concepts using its five strongest selected solution principles. Workflow condition, not a group of people (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Table 1).

participants.who: The human operators were the authors. No recruited human participant sample or count of people analyzed is reported; production counts concern AI-generated ideas and solution concepts, and the model agents are not people.
participants.quote: The experimental framework was built around a conversational, iterative dialogue between the AI-agents and human operators (i.e., the authors).
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 481), section 3, experimental framework; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 484), section 4, reports idea counts rather than participant counts.

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI ChatGPT-4o; OpenAI ChatGPT-o1; Google Gemini Advanced
ai_tool.how_used: Author-operated, structured conversational workflow: refine the problem, select inventive principles, generate ideas, synthesize concepts under the sequential approaches, rate concepts, cross-evaluate other agents’ outputs, and select the strongest concepts. Human operators monitored, clarified, approved stages, and selected core ideas for some approaches (PDF pp. 3–4, printed pp. 481–482, section 3 and Table 1).

task.description: Generate and refine concepts for mechanical engineering problems with known patented control solutions. The detailed illustrative case asks for a reusable twist-off screw cap that is easier to open without additional tools or disadvantages to manufacturers or consumers. The paper reports a unified series of cases but does not state the total number of design problems (PDF pp. 3–4, printed pp. 481–482, sections 3–4).

contrasts.reported: Approach 4 (human-selected core ideas enhanced with AI-selected complementary ideas): highest average Total Value, 4.20. Approach 1 (AI-agent merging complementary ideas): lowest average Total Value, 3.80. The composite combines AI ratings of usefulness, feasibility, complexity, and novelty. These are AI-generated concept scores; no denominator, SD, SE, confidence interval, or significance test is reported for the approach-level comparison.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 487), section 5, first paragraph, for the approach means; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 486), equation (1), and PDF p. 5 (printed p. 483), Table 2, for the composite and rating criteria.

outcomes.name: Share of strongest solution concepts by creation approach
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Approaches 2 and 5 (AI-selected core ideas or inventive principles) jointly accounted for nearly 60% of the strongest solution concepts; Approach 3 (human-selected core ideas) contributed approximately 22%. The first percentage combines two approaches. Counts, the denominator, and uncertainty are not reported for these percentages.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 486), section 5, final paragraph; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 482), section 3, Phase 5, describes AI selection of the strongest concepts.

eligibility.reason: Excluded as a model-only workflow comparison. For criterion 1, no human allocation mechanism is stated: the explicit sequential order concerns approaches applied to AI-agents (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, section 3, Phase 4 and Table 1), and the authors are described as human operators (PDF p. 3, printed p. 481, section 3). Criterion 2 cannot be established because no analyzed person count is given; reported production counts are ideas, not people (PDF p. 6, printed p. 484, section 4). Output scoring exists, but criterion 3 of the codebook requires output from a human participant sample: this paper rates AI-generated concepts (PDF p. 4, printed p. 482, Phase 4; PDF p. 7, printed p. 485, Tables 5–6). It therefore does not establish an eligible human experiment or context comparison.

one_line_finding: In this model-only comparison, AI-generated concepts built from human-selected core ideas plus AI-selected complementary ideas had average Total Value 4.20, versus 3.80 for AI-combined complementary ideas (PDF p. 9, printed p. 487, section 5).
